TCSlib

TCSlib

A Lean 4 Formalization of

Theoretical Computer Science

TCSlib is an open-source library formalizing results across theoretical computer science using Lean 4 and Mathlib. Our work spans Boolean function analysis and hypercontractivity, error-correcting codes, cryptography, and an ongoing formalization of Arora and Barak’s Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach.

Scripts and Tools for Lean Formalization

Have-to-Lemma

Extract local proof steps into reusable lemmas and clean up unnecessary intermediate facts. The tool uses Lean’s elaborated proof information and rechecks each rewrite before writing changes.

Use the have-to-lemma tool.

Proofmatch

Match reference statements and proofs from PDFs or validated Markdown to Lean declarations. Proofmatch supports source extraction, search, and comparison to help maintain auditable links between informal mathematics and formal proofs.

Explore Proofmatch.

Blueprints and Dependency Tools

Scripts extract declaration dependencies, generate and validate blueprint entries, and check style and attribution, keeping the informal exposition connected to the evolving library.

Browse the scripts.

Mathematics Dataset and Autoformalization Pipeline

Paired Informal and Formal Mathematics

Our dataset brings together TCSlib and attributed FABL material, pairing informal statements and proof accounts with extracted Lean statements, flattened proofs, dependency information, and source provenance. It is designed to support training and evaluation for autoformalization.

From Sources to Dataset

An incremental pipeline ingests references, matches citations, maintains blueprints, and generates statement prose and proof accounts where sources are unmatched. Cached stages support resuming work as the library grows.

Follow the pipeline guide.

Provenance and Validation

Published gzip shards and a manifest make the dataset accessible with checksums and project provenance. Structural checks and optional sampled Lean checks track quality; the proof-completeness flag records the absence of placeholders in extracted text and is separate from kernel validation.

Explore the dataset and schema.

Boolean Function Analysis

Fourier Analysis on the Hypercube

Foundations of Boolean function analysis over \{-1,1\}^n, including the Fourier expansion, Parseval's identity, and spectral norms.

Hypercontractivity Beyond the Cube

General forward and reverse noise inequalities, finite-product hypercontractivity, tensorization, and random-variable moment bounds.

Structure and Applications

Hypercontractive methods connect small-set expansion, low-degree concentration and anticoncentration, influences, and KKL. The library also includes Arrow’s impossibility theorem via Boolean function analysis.

Explore the development.

Complexity Theory

Models of Computation

An ongoing formalization of Arora and Barak’s textbook, built on reusable Turing-machine constructions, circuits, formulas, and simulations.

Complexity Classes and Reductions

Developments cover P, NP, PSPACE, NP-completeness and Cook–Levin, as well as space complexity, diagonalization, and hierarchy theorems.

An Active Formalization

Work continues across oracle computation, randomized complexity, circuit complexity, and expanders, with both completed proofs and open obligations.

Read the progress notes.

Cryptography

Secret Sharing

Shamir’s threshold scheme, reconstruction, and perfect privacy, with reusable foundations for access structures and shared secrets.

Identification and Public-Key Cryptography

Our cryptography work includes RSA and the Schnorr identification protocol, with completeness, witness extraction, and honest-verifier zero-knowledge results.

Secure Multiparty Computation

Ongoing work on arithmetic circuits and the BGW protocol over Shamir sharings connects secret sharing to secure distributed computation.

Explore cryptography.

Error-Correcting Codes

Classical Bounds

The Singleton, Hamming, Gilbert–Varshamov, and Johnson bounds on the parameters of error-correcting codes over arbitrary alphabets.

Linear Codes

Formal treatment of linear codes: generator and parity-check matrices, dual codes, and the MacWilliams identity.

Quantum Codes

Quantum Singleton and Quantum Hamming bounds, formalizing the fundamental limits of quantum error correction.
